links.comparator_used: Existing RAI-C scoring weights (calibrated 2010-2014, static) versus recalibrated parameter weights, tested in UPMC and VHA cohorts
links.outcome: Discrimination (c-statistic) and calibration for 180-day all-cause mortality
links.effect: UPMC c = 0.868 (95% CI 0.864-0.872) existing vs 0.872 (0.868-0.876) recalibrated; VHA c = 0.827 (0.822-0.832) existing vs 0.839 (0.834-0.845) recalibrated. Calibration improved slightly at the extremes, with little change near the frailty threshold. Reclassifying one additional patient as frail would require screening 1400-6000 patients.
links.tradeoff: Authors judge the resources needed to disseminate and implement a revised scoring system are not justified by the minimal gain. Recalibration also produced some multicollinearity-driven instability in the cancer diagnosis weights.
links.quote: The minimal incremental improvement associated with recalibration does not justify the resources required to disseminate and implement a revised scoring system.

design_hint: recalibration and drift monitoring of a deployed risk score
